paragraphs: Ravi, a pen pal in Singapore, sent Leo an email with a story. "My grandpa told me this story when I was small," he wrote. Leo read it to Mia in the school library. Mia listened with her chin on her hand.

Long ago, a camel and a tortoise lived in a hot desert. The camel was fast, and he was very proud. He laughed at the tortoise every day. "You are so slow," he said. "I do not like to hurry," said the tortoise. "I like to look at everything."

One year, there was no rain, and the water was gone. The sun was hot, and the sand was dry. The camel and the tortoise had to search for a stream. The camel ran across the hot sand all day. He did not look at the ground, and he did not find water. At night, he was tired, thirsty, and angry. The tortoise walked slowly and looked at the ground. She saw small green grass under a big rock.

"Grass needs water," said the tortoise. "Come with me." "I do not believe you," said the camel. The tortoise explained, "Look at the ground. Green grass is a sign. The water is near." The camel was very tired, so he followed her. Behind the rock, there was a small, cool stream. They drank the cold water for a long time. Then the camel felt better. "Thank you," said the camel. "I was wrong to laugh at you." "Slow and careful is not bad," said the tortoise with a smile. After that day, the camel never laughed at her again.

Leo looked at Mia. "What is the theme?" he asked. "Do not laugh at other people," said Mia. "And look carefully before you run." Leo began a cartoon of the camel and the tortoise. Mia liked the tortoise best.
